title: Audit export beta: per-tenant feature flag + rollout safety checks (allowlist/denylist, staged rollout)
author: Connor O'Brien
description:
Context: SIEM-ready audit export is going out as a gated beta. We need a hard per-tenant gate + rollout safety checks so we can safely canary, pause, and recover without relying on Console-only hiding.

What this PR does: (1) Adds a per-tenant feature flag `siem_audit_export_beta` to the control plane feature flag service (default OFF). (2) Adds rollout guardrails for audit export APIs (destination CRUD + health endpoints) that enforce allowlist/denylist + staged rollout semantics. (3) Adds an operator/admin endpoint to manage allow/deny entries and a read-only endpoint to introspect why a tenant is/ is not eligible (for Support/SRE triage). (4) Adds metrics + structured audit logs for flag evaluation outcomes.

Rollout policy (beta): denylist always wins; otherwise allowlist OR staged rollout grant. Staged rollout is keyed by tenant_id hash to ensure stability (no flapping) and is configurable by environment (staging: 100%, prod: 0% initially). We can move prod to 1%/5%/25% once SLOs look good.

Enforcement: control plane APIs return 404 for non-eligible tenants to reduce info leakage and prevent probing. For eligible tenants without the Console feature enabled, the Console still hides the page, but server-side checks are authoritative.

Notes: This does not change audit event delivery semantics or connector behavior; it only gates access + adds safety rails. This also does not introduce billing/packaging checks (that’s tracked separately in PM-4824).

Testing: unit tests for precedence (deny > allow > staged), stable hashing, and API behavior. Added integration test coverage for admin mutations + audit log emission.

Operator docs: updated internal runbook snippet in `ops/feature_flags.md` with recommended staged rollout steps and rollback guidance.
commits: control-plane/flags: add `siem_audit_export_beta` feature flag definition + default config
audit-export/api: gate destination CRUD + health behind tenant flag guard
flags: implement stable staged rollout evaluator (hash-based) + precedence rules
admin: add allowlist/denylist management endpoints + audit logging
metrics: add counters for eligibility decisions + denial reasons
conversation:
Priya Natarajan (review): Can we ensure denylist overrides allowlist and staged rollout in *all* code paths (including the admin introspection endpoint)? I don’t want any ambiguity when we need to emergency-stop a tenant.

Connor O'Brien (author): Yep. Precedence is centralized in the evaluator. I’ll add explicit tests for introspection + a comment in the route handler.

Connor O'Brien (author, push): Added `admin_feature_flags_introspection_precedence.test.ts` and moved the introspection endpoint to call the same evaluator used by request gating.

Marcus Lin (review): Two notes: (1) returning 404 makes sense for external callers, but make sure Support has a way to see *why* it’s blocked; (2) please confirm these admin endpoints are RBAC’d to internal-only roles.

Connor O'Brien (author): (1) Added `/admin/feature-flags/tenants/:tenant_id/decisions` (internal-only) which returns `enabled`, `reason`, and the matched rule source. (2) Admin routes are behind `internal_admin` permission; added a regression test to ensure non-admin tokens get 403.

Sean Gallagher (review): For staged rollout, do we have a metric that lets us see how many tenants are gated by each reason? Will help during canary.

Connor O'Brien (author): Added `feature_flag_decision_total{flag,result,reason}` counter + dashboard stub wiring (separate PR will add full dashboard panels). Also added log field `feature_flag_reason` on denial.

Naomi Feldman (review): Can you add a note in the PR description / docs about beta enablement expectations (prod remains 0% until we’ve onboarded design partners)?

Connor O'Brien (author): Updated `ops/feature_flags.md` with the recommended staged rollout sequence and explicit “prod=0% until PM signoff” guidance.

Chloe Martin (review): Does this impact Console? We should avoid the Console showing “permission denied” errors if a tenant navigates to the page.

Connor O'Brien (author): No Console changes here. Server returns 404 for non-enabled tenants. Console stays behind its own flag, but even if a user deep-links, they’ll get a not-found instead of a permission error.
release_notes: Internal: Added per-tenant gating for SIEM-ready audit export beta, with allowlist/denylist and staged rollout support. No customer-visible behavior change unless enabled for a tenant.
